heard: Think the moon doesn't spin, that is a total myth. The moon actually rotates on its axis at the exact same speed it orbits our home planet. This cosmic synchronization keeps the exact same side facing Earth forever. Earth's immense gravity constantly stretches the moon into tidal bulges that generate gravitational torque. In 1959, the Soviet spacecraft Luna 3 successfully transmitted the very first photographs of the far side. This tidal locking is precisely why humanity never caught a single glimpse of that hidden hemisphere before. Because tidal locking ensures the moon's rotation matches its orbit, you have to wonder if it ever stays still.
